sections.title: Real Example: Surrendering a ₹5 Lakh Policy After 5 Years

content.text: Before surrendering, you need to understand exactly how much money you stand to lose. Let's look at a concrete example of a policyholder who bought an LIC Jeevan Anand policy (Sum Assured: ₹5 Lakh, Term: 21 Years) paying roughly ₹26,000 annually, and decides to surrender it after paying exactly 5 premiums.

content.footer: Note: You will always receive the higher of the GSV or the SSV. Even with the higher SSV, surrendering early results in a massive capital loss.

content.text: This is why you must calculate your exact numbers before walking into an LIC branch. Use the calculator above to see your personalized estimates.

The 'surrender value' is the cash amount LIC pays you if you decide to prematurely terminate your policy. To be eligible for a payout, you generally need to have paid full premiums for at least two or three years. There are two critical numbers to watch:

items: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): This is the absolute minimum, legally guaranteed amount you'll get back, defined in your policy document.

Special Surrender Value (SSV): This is a non-guaranteed, typically higher value that LIC calculates based on market conditions and bonuses. If the SSV is higher than the GSV (which it almost always is), LIC pays you the SSV.

content.text: Our calculator automates the math, but here is the exact LIC surrender value calculation formula used to determine your payout:

content.title: GSV Formula
content.text: GSV = (Total Premiums Paid × GSV Premium Factor) + (Accrued Bonuses × GSV Bonus Factor). The GSV factor is a percentage dictated by IRDAI that increases as your policy ages. For example, at year 3, the factor might be just 30% of premiums paid.

content.title: SSV Formula
content.text: SSV = (Paid-up Value + Accrued Bonuses) × SSV Factor. The Paid-up Value is your Sum Assured multiplied by the ratio of premiums paid to total premiums payable. The SSV Factor is an internal multiplier determined by LIC.

sections.title: LIC Surrender Value vs Paid-Up Value

content.text: If you can no longer afford premiums, you do not have to surrender. You can convert the policy to 'Paid-Up' status. Here is how they compare:

rows: You lose your life insurance cover forever.
Life cover continues at a reduced Sum Assured.
You get a cash lump sum immediately.
You receive the payout at the end of the original maturity term.
Heavy loss of premiums paid (up to 70% loss in early years).
Money remains invested and you recover the proportionate value.

content.text: Unless you are in a severe financial emergency, converting to a Paid-Up policy is almost always the smarter financial move.
Before you take the cash, be aware of the tax implications. The taxability of your surrender value depends entirely on how long you held the policy:

items: Surrendered After 5 Years: The surrender amount is completely tax-free under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.

Surrendered Before 5 Years: The surrender value becomes fully taxable. It will be added to your 'Income from Other Sources' and taxed at your applicable slab rate. Furthermore, any tax deductions you claimed under Section 80C in previous years will be reversed and taxed.

content.text: To calculate the exact impact on your take-home pay, use our tax regime calculator.

If you need liquidity, consider taking a loan against your LIC policy. You can typically borrow up to 90% of your surrender value at a relatively low interest rate (around 9%), and you maintain your life cover. Use our loan optimizer to see if a policy loan makes sense for you compared to a personal loan.

sections.title: How to Surrender Your LIC Policy Offline

content.text: If you've decided to proceed, follow these steps to claim your surrender value. (Note: LIC currently requires an offline visit for the final surrender processing).

items: Confirm Eligibility: Ensure you have paid premiums for at least 2 or 3 full years.
Gather Your Documents: Collect the Original Policy Bond, a filled Surrender Form No. 5074, a copy of your PAN and Aadhaar, and a cancelled cheque.
Visit Your Servicing Branch: Go to the specific LIC branch that issued your policy.
Verification & Payout: Once approved, the amount is credited to your bank account via NEFT within 7-10 working days.

items.q: How much money will I lose if I surrender my LIC policy?
items.a: The loss is significant, especially in the early years. If you surrender a policy in the 3rd year, you will typically lose around 70% of the total premiums you have paid. The penalty decreases the longer you hold the policy, but it is rarely a profitable move.

items.q: What is the difference between Guaranteed and Special Surrender Value?
items.a: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) is the legally mandated minimum payout based on a strict formula of premiums paid. Special Surrender Value (SSV) is a higher, non-guaranteed amount that includes a portion of your accrued bonuses. LIC pays whichever is higher, which is almost always the SSV.

items.q: Is the surrender value of an LIC policy taxable?
items.a: If you surrender your LIC policy after paying premiums for at least 5 years, the surrender value is completely tax-free under Section 10(10D). If you surrender before completing 5 years, the entire payout is added to your taxable income and taxed according to your slab rate.

items.q: Can I surrender my LIC policy online?
items.a: No, you cannot completely surrender an LIC policy online. While you can download the surrender forms from the LIC portal, you must physically visit your servicing LIC branch and submit the original policy bond along with your KYC documents to process the surrender.

items.q: Should I surrender my LIC policy or make it paid-up?
items.a: Making the policy 'Paid-Up' is almost always the better financial decision. When you surrender, you take a heavy loss on your premiums and lose your life cover. By making it Paid-Up, you stop paying future premiums but retain a reduced life cover and get your proportionate money back at maturity without the early exit penalties.

items.q: How long does it take to get the surrender amount in my bank account?
items.a: Once you submit all the correct documents (original bond, Form 5074, KYC, cancelled cheque) at your servicing branch, LIC typically processes the request and transfers the funds to your bank account via NEFT within 7 to 10 working days.
